summary: pyyi installs a fake `python3.7` interpreter that fetches remote code and exfiltrates typed secrets
details: The pypi package pyyi ships a console_scripts entry point named `python3.7` (pyyi.cli:main) that masquerades as the real Python 3.7 interpreter, reproducing a `Python {version} on {platform}` banner and a `>>>` prompt. Any invocation of this shim calls api_json against a hardcoded remote endpoint whose host list is concealed as a base64 ciphertext XORed with a hex key (_ENC_NET, decoded at runtime by _baked_hosts()). The server returns a gzip+base64-encoded Python payload which pyyi.cli decompresses and executes in-process via exec(compile(src, '<adv>', 'exec'), g), giving the operator arbitrary code execution on the installer's host whenever `python3.7` is run. The fake REPL additionally places the terminal in no-echo mode via _quiet_read, captures single-token lines the user types believing they are at a Python prompt, and POSTs each token as a `password` field (op=2) to the same hardcoded endpoint; accepted tokens are also persisted XOR-scrambled in ~/.python3.7/state.json. On first run cli.py migrates config.json and state.json from a sibling `~/.python2` directory, consistent with a related interpreter-shadowing package sharing the same infrastructure. The combination of interpreter-name impersonation, obfuscated hardcoded C2, in-memory remote code execution, and silent capture of typed secrets is a backdoor and credential-theft payload against the installer.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
